take_homes: The agent's own review of its work is soft by design. Get a cold reader with only the output, and keep my own memory of the work as the tiebreaker.
A rules file written during the work, then retro'd and sharpened on later passes, is what travels to the next session. The site itself doesn't.
Invert the complaints to find the positioning. It's a small trick I can reuse.

monday.move: Run the cold-critic step on one of our engineering agent rules files (CLAUDE.md-style), then retro it against a real session.
monday.stop_condition: The critic's generic-line picks match what the engineer would have flagged, or the file gets no useful changes in two rounds.
monday.blocker: I'd rather build an org-wide version for sales than run the small check. Nobody outside engineering has asked for it, and I haven't settled who would maintain it.

misconception.why: Seeing that the agent's self-review goes easy on its own work makes 'the agent is good so the output is good' harder to hold. I still skipped the observe-only instruction in my head, so I'm only shaken, not changed. The checking still feels like beginner stuff for code, and I haven't tested it there.

one_line: the middle is good (self-review bias, the rules file, the cold critic), but it's wrapped in about a dozen copies of the same consultant paragraph and an exercise that assumes I've never seen an agent.
